pages.text: A spell program is a directed acyclic graph.$(br2)Each node is a rune. Each edge connects one rune output to one named input on another rune. A graph has exactly one output node.

pages.title: MVP Types
pages.text: $(li)Unit$(li)Bool$(li)Number$(li)Vec3$(li)Entity$(li)Player$(li)BlockPos$(li)RayHit$(br2)A Number output cannot feed a Vec3 input unless a rune explicitly converts it.

pages.title: Reading A Proof
pages.text: Theorem nodes read $(thing)#n Rune -> type$(). The number is a stable reference within that displayed proof.$(br2)Hover a node to see each named input bound to its source, the final-result marker, constants, and exact technical ids. Type-colored marks show what each rune produces.

pages.title: Output Families
pages.text: The four-square mark in a graph header explains output domains: $(gold)scalar and logic$(), $(aqua)space and geometry$(), $(blue)actors$(), and $(red)effects$().$(br2)The color is a quick family cue, not the exact type. Hover the mark for its legend; read the node's arrow for the precise type.
